lab_tasks.instruction: Open state-compliant.json and, before running anything, write down in words the binary control claim and which observable fields decide it; then read ccm-check.sh and find the line where a bucket is judged compliant only if all four flags are true, and reconcile the stated claim with the code's logic.
lab_tasks.objective: O1/O2 — translate a fuzzy policy into a sharp binary observable claim and map it to evaluation code
lab_tasks.machine_verify_check: Free-text answer graded by keyword/structured match: claim names the population (every S3 bucket), the four flags (block_public_acls, block_public_policy, ignore_public_acls, restrict_public_buckets), and binary pass/fail semantics; learner identifies the awk condition $2=="true" && $3=="true" && $4=="true" && $5=="true" (or the bun flag() equivalent) as the compliance test. In a sim: multiple-choice or click-the-line-of-code selection in a read-only code viewer.

lab_tasks.instruction: source ./ccm-lab/ccm-check.sh, run evaluate_control labs/fixtures/state-compliant.json, inspect $?, and state in one sentence what the exit code means and why the loop branches on it rather than on the printed text.
lab_tasks.objective: O2/O3 — verdict via exit code; exit code is the machine-facing contract
lab_tasks.machine_verify_check: Terminal sim verifies the learner ran evaluate_control on the compliant fixture and then 'echo $?' showing 0; sim state records last_exit_code==0 and that the PASS line 'PASS control=CC6.1-s3-public-access-block evaluated=3 noncompliant=0' was displayed. One-sentence answer checked for 'exit code 0 = control holds / machines branch on exit code'.

lab_tasks.instruction: Run emit_evidence labs/fixtures/state-compliant.json ./ccm-lab/evidence; open the run-*.evidence record and the new ledger.log row; confirm NO alert-*.txt was created; explain why storing a passing record is not redundant.
lab_tasks.objective: O3/O4 — evidence on every run; proof of the negative
lab_tasks.machine_verify_check: Sim filesystem check: evidence/run-20260520090000.evidence exists with exit_code=0 and verdict=PASS line, ledger.log has exactly 1 row containing 'rc=0', and zero files matching alert-*.txt. lab_tasks.instruction: Build the dashboard tile as a query over the ledger: write one or two lines using tail/awk/grep on ledger.log that print the current verdict (latest row) and a 30-day strip of pass/fail markers; confirm the tile shows the drift as a single red interval after a run of green, and explain why the strip is evidence the bare current state is not.
lab_tasks.objective: O4 — dashboard tile is a query over the append-only store, not a separately maintained status

lab_setup_state: Learner runs `bash labs/setup.sh ./ccm-lab`, which generates ./ccm-lab/ccm-check.sh (a sourceable bash function library defining normalize_buckets, evaluate_control, emit_evidence — pure bash + coreutils + awk, optional bun for JSON parsing, no jq/cloud/network/Docker) and an empty ./ccm-lab/evidence/ directory. Four committed fixtures live at labs/fixtures/: state-compliant.json (3 buckets, all four public-access-block flags true, captured_at 2026-05-20T09:00:00Z), state-drifted.json (same 3 buckets but acme-public-website has all four flags false, captured_at 2026-05-21T09:00:00Z), state-drifted-pretty.json (identical drift but pretty-printed multi-line JSON, captured_at 2026-05-22T09:00:00Z — regression fixture for the fail-open same-line-parsing bug), and state-empty.json (zero buckets, captured_at 2026-05-23T09:00:00Z — must fail closed with exit 2). The control under monitoring is CC6.1-s3-public-access-block: 'every S3 bucket has all four public-access-block flags enabled'. Evidence artifacts produced during the lab: run-<digits-of-captured_at>.evidence records (key=value lines: control_id, captured_at, verdict, exit_code, source_state), append-only ledger.log (one row per run: '<captured_at> <run_id> rc=<n> <verdict line>'), and alert-run-*.txt files only on non-zero runs.
assessment_artifact: 60-minute unaided competency artifact against a FRESH unseen control claim and a fresh pair of snapshots (assessor copies the lab fixtures then hand-edits so a DIFFERENT bucket drifts and optionally a different flag set is required). Learner delivers: (1) a working CCM loop — check that reads captured state, prints PASS/FAIL, returns correct exit code (0 pass / non-zero drift), emits a dated evidence record on EVERY run; (2) a populated append-only history store with records for both runs plus a dashboard tile (a query over the store) showing current verdict + trailing-30-day trend; (3) a drift alert that fired only on the drifted run naming control, drifted resource, and timestamp; (4) a written walkthrough covering snapshot-vs-monitor, what the exit code drives, the proof-of-the-negative argument for passing evidence, why the trend tile is evidence a status light is not, and a stage-by-stage own-vs-rent decision naming one vendor claim refused as evidence. Rubric: 6 Pass/Not-yet rows (snapshot vs monitor §3/§4.1; five-part loop §3/§4.8; check + exit-code verdict §4.2-4.4; evidence store + dashboard §4.4-4.6; diagnosing drift §4.7/§5.3; build-vs-buy §4.8/§5.4); all rows must Pass; a Not-yet routes to the named section only.

exercise_design.sim_state: A simulated lab directory: ./ccm-lab/ccm-check.sh (read-only, the real committed library text), ./ccm-lab/evidence/ (starts empty, mutated by emit_evidence), and labs/fixtures/{state-compliant,state-drifted,state-drifted-pretty,state-empty}.json (exact committed contents). The terminal sim implements bash builtins plus the lab's contract: source, evaluate_control, emit_evidence, echo $?, ls, cat, tail, head, grep, awk, wc, diff. evaluate_control and emit_evidence are pure functions of (fixture name) -> (exact stdout/stderr, exit code, file-system mutations) so every output can be replayed byte-identically from the verified transcript: PASS/FAIL/ERROR lines, run-*.evidence contents, ledger.log appends, alert-*.txt creation. Additionally seed an extended 31-row ledger.log variant (30 rc=0 rows then 1 rc=1 row) for the dashboard-tile task so the 30-day strip is meaningful. A simulated 'scheduler + cloud console' state for the capstone: bucket flag toggles + a time-advance button that re-runs the loop.
exercise_design.notes: This module is unusually well-suited to high-fidelity simulation because the real lab is already offline-by-construction (committed fixtures, deterministic bash, no cloud). Best design: a 9-step terminal-sim narrative mirroring lab tasks 1-7 plus two additions. Steps: (1) matching/claim-builder — assemble the binary control claim from population/property/predicate parts and click the judging line in a read-only ccm-check.sh viewer; (2) run evaluate_control on the compliant fixture and echo $? (exact verbatim output, exit 0); (3) emit_evidence compliant run — then ls/cat to verify record + ledger row + no alert (filesystem assertions); (4) induce drift with state-drifted.json — read the alert and answer three structured fields (control / resource / timestamp) auto-graded exactly; (5) edge-case step unique to this module's hardening story: run evaluate_control on state-drifted-pretty.json (must still FAIL — teaches the fail-open parsing bug) and state-empty.json (exit 2, fail closed — teaches refusing vacuous green); (6) dashboard tile: free-form awk/tail pipeline over the pre-seeded 31-row ledger graded on output contract (latest verdict + one marker per row, 30 green then 1 red), with a rendered dashboard-sim tile that updates live from the learner's query; (7) determinism: run the drifted evaluation twice and diff; (8) simulated scheduler capstone replacing optional task 8 — toggle a bucket flag in a mini cloud-console panel, advance the clock so the cron tick re-runs emit_evidence, and watch the alert fire; (9) structured-builder build-vs-buy memo: six own/rent rows + refused-vendor-claim field. Every terminal output is replayable verbatim from the real library run, so fidelity is exact.

fidelity_notes: All core outputs verified by actually running setup.sh + ccm-check.sh on this host (bash + awk + bun present) — PASS/FAIL/ERROR lines, evidence records, ledger rows, and alert files reproduce byte-identically to module §5 examples, so terminal-sim fidelity can be exact. Caveats: (1) run_id derives from the fixture's captured_at timestamp (run-20260520090000), but for state-empty-like snapshots lacking captured_at the library falls back to wall-clock UTC — sim should pin a fake clock; note state-empty.json DOES carry captured_at 2026-05-23T09:00:00Z so its run_id is deterministic (run-20260523090000). (2) Module §5.1/§5.3 show 'exit_code: 0' / 'exit_code: 1' as a stylized caption — the real command output is just the PASS/FAIL lines; the exit code is only visible via $? or in the evidence record as 'exit_code=0'. (3) The §5.4 dashboard tile (emoji strip, 'held green for 30 days') is authored illustration, not produced by any committed command — lab task 5 has the learner write their own tail/awk one-liner, so grade on output contract rather than exact text, and pre-seed a 31-row ledger to make the strip non-trivial (the real lab only produces 2 rows). (4) The bun parser and the pure-awk fallback produce identical normalized rows for all four fixtures (same-output contract), so the sim need not model both. (5) The empty-snapshot ERROR line goes to stderr while the FAIL line goes to stdout — a sim that merges streams should preserve ordering (ERROR first). (6) Lab task 8 (real cloud + cron + alert channel) cannot be reproduced statically; replace with the simulated scheduler/console interaction. (7) evaluate_control exit code 2 (fail closed) vs 1 (drift) is a deliberate distinction the sim must preserve, including the alert text 'drifted_resource=<none — evaluated 0 resources; snapshot empty, unparsed, or wrong shape>' for rc=2 runs.
